cards: King Wu was the founding king of the Zhou dynasty.
d. c. 1043 BCE · Central & East Asia
The Duke of Zhou, Ji Dan, was a brother of King Wu, founder of the Zhou dynasty.
Di Xin was the last king of the Shang dynasty of China.
King Wen of Zhou was the leader of the Zhou people in the Wei River valley in the late Shang period.
d. c. 1050 BCE · Central & East Asia
Jiang Ziya, also known as Jiang Taigong, was a minister and military adviser to Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou in the eleventh century BCE.
King Cheng of Zhou was the second king of the Western Zhou, son of King Wu.
r. c. 1042–1021 BCE · Central & East Asia
Tiglath-Pileser I was king of Assyria from about 1114 to 1076 BCE.
r. c. 1114–1076 BCE · Ancient Near East
Ramesses XI was the last pharaoh of the Twentieth Dynasty and of the Egyptian New Kingdom.
d. c. 1070 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Ahiram was a king of Byblos, known from his stone sarcophagus found in the city's royal necropolis in 1923.
r. c. 1000 BCE · Ancient Near East
The Duke of Shao, personal name Ji Shi, was a senior member of the Zhou royal house who helped King Wu overthrow the Shang.
Herihor was an Egyptian army officer who became High Priest of Amun at Thebes around 1080 BCE, in the last years of Ramesses XI and the Twentieth Dynasty.
fl. c. 1080 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Smendes was a ruler of Lower Egypt from Tanis at the end of the New Kingdom, who founded the Twenty-First Dynasty.
r. c. 1077–1052 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Daji was the favourite consort of Di Xin, last king of the Shang dynasty, in traditional Chinese histories.
Di Yi was the penultimate king of the Shang dynasty and father of Di Xin, the last Shang king.
Zakar-Baal was a king of Byblos around 1075 BCE, known from the Egyptian Story of Wenamun.
r. c. 1075 BCE · Ancient Near East
Cai Shu Du was a son of King Wen of Zhou and brother of King Wu, who gave him the fief of Cai in Henan.
Marduk-nadin-ahhe was a king of Babylon of the Second Dynasty of Isin, reigning from about 1099 to 1082 BCE, and a brother of Nebuchadnezzar I.
r. c. 1099–1082 BCE · Ancient Near East
Nahash was a king of Ammon in the late 11th or early 10th century BCE, known from the Hebrew Bible.
fl. c. 1000 BCE · Ancient Near East
Panehesy was viceroy of Kush under Ramesses XI, the last king of Egypt's Twentieth Dynasty.
fl. c. 1080 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Pinedjem I was High Priest of Amun at Thebes from about 1070 to 1032 BCE, during the Twenty-first Dynasty.
fl. c. 1070–1032 BCE · Egypt & North Africa
Psusennes I was a king of the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt who ruled from Tanis in the late 11th century BCE for about 46 years.
Shu Yu of Tang was a son of King Wu of Zhou and younger brother of King Cheng, who received the fief of Tang in southern Shanxi in the 11th century BCE.
